holding_summary: A city building inspector sought to enjoin an owner from continuing alterations of a back building into four separate tenement dwellings that lacked the open-space and street-width margins required for 'new' buildings under the Act of 1855. The court held the alterations did constitute a new building subject to the light-and-air requirements and ordered the rooms reopened to destroy their separate character, but held the statute gave courts no power to restrict the owner's right to let the building, once conforming, to one or several tenants as he chose.
